text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Banking and insurance sector is the only Dutch business sector in which employment is expected to decrease this year and next. (p1)
- Brewer Heineken sees recovery this year after last year's slight dip in profit. (p1)
- Government prosecutor calls for conclusions of report on bourse supervision over brokerage firm Nusse Brink. (p1)
- Building concern Volker Stevin posts 25 percent higher 1996 net profit of Dfl 73 million. (p3)
- Builder Kondor Wessels reports profits in first half of 1996/97 book year up 18 pct to 15.4 million guilders. (p3)
- Publisher Wolters Kluwer saw profit margins narrow last year. (p3)
- Content Beheer, temp agency and training institute firm, gets permission from education ministry to start its own higher vocational college HBO. (p4)
- Automotive group Athlon reckons with further profits growth in 1997. (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Social fund administrator GAK Nederland trumps real estate fund Capa City and Larmag by buying 38 office buildings. (p2)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM places order with U.S. aircraft maker Boeing for four 737-800 aircraft. (p2)
- PM Wim Kok pressures environment minister Magaretha de Boer and minister of economy Hans Wijers to make haste with new environmental policy. (p6)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Coalition parties want junior ministers of justice and finance to introduce a licence system for pyramid games. (p3)
- Dutch oil exploration company NAM receives 150 damages claims after earth tremor of February 19. (p4)
- Bank insurer ING group to invest more in realty to correct proportions of its investment portfolio. (p13)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Oil and chemicals sector in the Rotterdam Rijnmond area will have a shortage of 80-120 operators until 2000. (p11)
TROUW
- Surinam's president Jules Wijdenbosch says Surinam will no longer protect the Netherlands's good name in relation with drugs trafficking. (p1)
